breakfast.name: Halloumi and Eggs
instructions: Fry halloumi slices until golden
Fry eggs
Serve with sliced tomatoes, cucumber, olives, bread
breakfast.description: Cypriot breakfast of fried halloumi and eggs.

breakfast.name: Tahinopita (Tahini Pie)
ingredients: For dough: 3 cups flour, olive oil, water
Filling: 1 cup tahini, 1/2 cup sugar, cinnamon
instructions: Make oil-based dough, rest
Roll out, spread tahini-sugar filling
Roll up, coil into pan
Bake at 180°C 30 min

breakfast.name: Flaouna (Easter Cheese Pastry)
ingredients: Dough: flour, yeast, milk, olive oil, mahlab (cherry kernel spice), mastic
Filling: halloumi, cheddar, eggs, semolina, raisins, dried mint
instructions: Make aromatic dough with mahlab and mastic, rise 1 hour
Mix grated cheeses with eggs, semolina, raisins, mint
Shape dough into squares, fill generously
Fold corners over, leaving center open
Brush with egg, sprinkle sesame seeds
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 min until golden
breakfast.description: Aromatic cheese-filled pastry made for Easter — the mahlab and mastic in the dough give a distinctive flavor. Every Cypriot household bakes dozens.

lunch.name: Souvlaki with Pita
instructions: Marinate pork with oil, lemon, oregano, garlic
Thread on skewers
Grill over charcoal
Serve in pita with tzatziki, onions, tomatoes
lunch.description: Charcoal-grilled pork skewers in pita — the Cypriot lunch.

lunch.name: Sheftalia (Grilled Sausages)
instructions: Mix meats with onion, parsley, cinnamon
Shape into sausages
Wrap in caul fat
Grill over charcoal until cooked through
lunch.description: Herb-spiced sausages wrapped in caul fat and grilled.

lunch.name: Kolokasi (Taro Root Stew)
ingredients: 1kg kolokasi (taro root, peeled, broken into chunks)
instructions: Brown pork and onion
Add tomato paste, celery, stock
Break kolokasi into chunks by hand (never cut)
Add to stew
Simmer 40 min until taro is tender and sauce thick
Finish with lemon juice
lunch.description: Cyprus's signature stew — taro root and pork in lemony sauce. Taro must be broken by hand so the starch thickens the broth naturally.

dinner.name: Kleftiko (Slow-Baked Lamb)
instructions: Score lamb, insert garlic slivers
Season with lemon, oregano, salt, pepper
Place with potatoes in roasting pan
Cover tightly with foil
Bake at 160°C for 4 hours
Lamb should fall off bone
dinner.description: Stolen lamb — slow-baked until falling apart.

dinner.name: Koupepia (Stuffed Vine Leaves)
instructions: Mix meat with rice, onions, herbs, spices
Fill vine leaves, roll tightly
Pack in pot seam-down
Add water, tomato paste, lemon juice
Simmer 60 min
dinner.description: Cypriot-style stuffed vine leaves with pork and mint.

dinner.name: Ofton Kleftiko (Slow-Baked Lamb)
instructions: Insert garlic slices into cuts in lamb
Season with lemon juice, oregano, cinnamon, salt, pepper
Place lamb and potatoes in sealed vessel
Seal tightly — no steam should escape
Bake at 150°C for 4 hours
Do not open until serving — the lamb falls off the bone
dinner.description: Stolen lamb — named for bandits who slow-cooked lamb in sealed underground pits to hide the smoke. Sealed cooking concentrates all the flavor.

snacks.name: Koupes (Bulgur Croquettes)
ingredients: Filling: 250g pork mince, onion, parsley, cinnamon
instructions: Soak bulgur, knead into shell
Make spiced meat filling
Shape bulgur around filling into torpedoes
Deep fry until crispy
snacks.description: Crispy bulgur shells stuffed with spiced pork.

snacks.name: Halloumi Grilled
instructions: Brush halloumi with olive oil
Grill on high heat 2 min per side
Squeeze lemon over, sprinkle oregano and mint
Eat immediately while warm
snacks.description: Grilled halloumi — Cyprus's famous cheese that doesn't melt. The squeaky texture and salty char are addictive.

snacks.name: Halloumi Fries
instructions: Cut halloumi into thick fry shapes
Dust lightly in flour — helps the exterior crisp
Fry in hot oil 2-3 min per side until golden, or air-fry at 200°C for 8 min
The outside should be crispy, the inside squeaky and molten
Squeeze lemon juice over immediately
Sprinkle fresh mint
Optional: drizzle honey for a sweet-salty contrast
Eat immediately — halloumi hardens as it cools
snacks.description: Halloumi fries — the Cypriot cheese that doesn't melt, cut into fry shapes and fried until golden outside and squeaky-molten inside. The cheese that 'breaks the rules' went viral globally, and halloumi fries are now on menus from London to Sydney. Cyprus lobbied for and won EU protected status for the cheese.

desserts.name: Loukoumades (Honey Doughnuts)
instructions: Make batter, rise 1 hour
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until golden
Drizzle with honey
Top with cinnamon and walnuts
desserts.description: Puffy dough balls drizzled with honey — a Cypriot favorite.

desserts.name: Galaktoboureko (Custard Phyllo Pie)
ingredients: Custard: 1L milk, 150g semolina, 200g sugar, 4 eggs, vanilla, butter
Syrup: 300g sugar, 200ml water, lemon juice, cinnamon stick
instructions: Make custard: cook milk, semolina, sugar until thick, cool, beat in eggs
Layer phyllo in pan, brushing each with butter
Pour in custard, top with more buttered phyllo
Score top, bake at 180°C for 35-40 min
Make syrup: boil sugar, water, lemon, cinnamon
Pour cool syrup over hot pie
Let soak before serving
desserts.description: Crispy phyllo pie filled with semolina custard and drenched in syrup — Cypriot-Greek dessert at its most indulgent.

drinks.name: Cypriot Coffee
instructions: Add coffee, sugar, water to briki
Heat slowly, stirring
When foam rises, pour into cups
Serve with glass of water
drinks.description: Strong, thick coffee brewed in a briki.

drinks.name: Zivania (Grape Spirit)
instructions: Collect grape pomace after pressing
Distill in copper pot still
Distill twice for purity
Serve as aperitif or digestif
drinks.description: Potent grape pomace spirit — Cyprus's national drink.

drinks.name: Commandaria (Ancient Dessert Wine)
ingredients: Commandaria wine (from sun-dried Xynisteri and Mavro grapes)
instructions: Serve at room temperature or slightly chilled in small glasses
Sip slowly — it's rich, amber, and honeyed
drinks.description: The oldest named wine in the world — produced in Cyprus since 800 BC. Made from sun-dried grapes.
